$comment: Test fixture exercising all fields of the latin-america extension

brazilianSuccession.notes: Deceased was in a stable union (uniao estavel) recognised under Brazilian Civil Code art. 1723. Community property regime (comunhao parcial de bens) applies; meacao split performed before succession.

argentineSuccession.porcionDisponible: One-third of the estate available for free disposition
argentineSuccession.notes: Collation (colacion) required for lifetime gifts to forced heirs per Argentine Civil and Commercial Code art. 2385. Gift of Buenos Aires flat to eldest daughter must be brought into hotchpot.

colombianSuccession.legitimaRigurosa: First quarter: divided equally among forced heirs
colombianSuccession.cuartaDeMejoras: Second quarter: allocated to eldest son as mejora
colombianSuccession.cuartaDeLibreDisposicion: Fourth quarter: bequeathed to charitable foundation
colombianSuccession.notes: Colombian fourths system applied per Civil Code art. 1226. Testator allocated the cuarta de mejoras to the eldest son and the cuarta de libre disposicion to a registered charitable foundation in Bogota.

venezuelanSuccession.applicableLaw: Venezuelan Civil Code, Book III, Title II — Of Successions
venezuelanSuccession.notes: Legitima fraction of one half applies to descendants. Venezuelan law governs immovable property situated in Caracas regardless of domicile of the deceased.

notes: Comprehensive fixture covering all four Latin American succession sub-schemas. In practice, a single estate would typically populate only one country-specific section. This fixture populates all sections for full schema coverage testing.
